decisions.reason: Setting Danish as the default template language does not change bullet dimensions, balance, alignment, or scaling behavior.
The language configuration does not change the requirement that pasted content remain within column and page boundaries.
The default-language decision does not alter the identified legacy sources, migration target, or required copy-paste stability.
Using Danish as the default language does not change the required alignment and usability of numbered or multilevel lists.
The default-language setting does not change the required ability to insert manual line breaks after pasted content.
The Danish default-language decision does not alter the PBU style prefix, applicable styles, or naming condition.
The source establishes a separate language configuration and does not change the specified style system or its application coverage.
The language setting neither changes table-paste layout constraints nor resolves the existing table-adjustment ambiguity.
Setting the default language to Danish does not change Tab-driven level transitions, list applicability, hierarchy, or alignment.
The default-language configuration does not change the supported Microsoft Word environment or operational-reliability requirement.
